questions.prompt: What is the greatest area, in m², of a rectangle with perimeter 48 m?
questions.explanation: Let sides be x and 24−x, so A=24x−x². The derivative 24−2x vanishes at x=12, with negative second derivative. The maximum area is 12·12=144 m². Boundary limits have zero area, so the interior nondegenerate rectangle wins. A: This doubles the area instead of multiplying the two optimal side lengths. B: A 24 m by 24 m square would violate the perimeter constraint. C: This is the perimeter, not an area. D: The sides are 12 m and 12 m at the maximum.

questions.prompt: A rectangular pen against a straight river uses 80 m of fencing for its other three sides. What is its greatest possible area, in m²?
questions.explanation: With perpendicular side x, the remaining fenced side is 80−2x. Then A=80x−2x² and A′=80−4x, zero at x=20. The other side is 40, giving maximum area 800 m². The concave quadratic and zero boundary limits establish a global maximum. A: The perpendicular sides are 20 m each and the parallel fenced side is 40 m. B: This uses the square of the perpendicular length instead of multiplying by the parallel side. C: A 40 m by 40 m pen would require 120 m of three-side fencing. D: This is the fencing length, not the enclosed area.

questions.prompt: An open box is formed by cutting equal corner squares from a 12 cm square sheet and folding up the sides. What is its maximum volume, in cm³?
questions.explanation: The volume is V=x(12−2x)² for 0<x<6. Differentiate and factor: V′=(12−2x)(12−6x). The interior stationary cut is x=2, where V=2·8²=128 cm³. The volume tends to zero at both domain boundaries. A: This is only the optimal base area, omitting the height factor 2. B: Cut size 2 cm gives base 8 cm by 8 cm and height 2 cm. C: This is the volume at cut size 3 cm, not the optimum. D: This is the limiting volume at a degenerate endpoint, not the maximum.

questions.prompt: A closed cylinder has volume 16π cm³. What radius, in cm, minimizes its total surface area?
questions.explanation: From πr²h=16π, h=16/r². The closed-cylinder area is S=2πr²+32π/r. Its derivative is 4π(r³−8)/r², negative for 0<r<2 and positive for r>2. Thus the unique global minimum has r=2 cm and h=4 cm. A: This is the optimal height, not radius. B: This reports r³ without taking its cube root. C: The reduced area has derivative zero when r³=8, and decreases then increases across r=2. D: The surface-area derivative is not zero at this radius.

questions.prompt: Profit is P(q)=−2q²+120q−500 dollars for 0≤q≤50. What is the greatest profit, in dollars?
questions.explanation: The derivative P′=−4q+120 vanishes at q=30. The second derivative is −4, and P(30)=1300. Compare endpoints P(0)=−500 and P(50)=500; both are smaller. Hence the greatest profit is 1300 dollars. A: This omits the fixed cost 500. B: This is the maximizing input, not profit. C: This is the profit at zero production. D: The maximizing quantity is 30 and P(30)=−1800+3600−500.

questions.prompt: A point (x,x²), with −2≤x≤2, is chosen closest to (0,1). What is the minimum squared distance?
questions.explanation: Squared distance is D²=x²+(x²−1)²=x⁴−x²+1. Its derivative is 2x(2x²−1), giving candidates 0 and ±1/√2 along with endpoints. At the two nonzero stationary inputs, D²=1/2+1/4=3/4, smaller than 1 at 0 or 13 at either endpoint. A: The squared-distance polynomial has minima at x=±1/√2. B: This is the squared distance at x=0, a nonoptimal candidate. C: This omits the squared vertical separation at the optimum. D: The point (0,1) does not lie on the parabola.

questions.prompt: Angles are in radians. What is the maximum value of sin x+cos x on [0,π/2]?
questions.explanation: The derivative is cos x−sin x, zero at π/4 in the interval. Endpoint values are both 1, while the interior value is √2. The second derivative is −sin x−cos x<0 on the interval interior, confirming the maximum. A: This is the value at either endpoint. B: The stationary input π/4 gives two contributions √2/2. C: Sine and cosine cannot both equal 1 at the same input. D: Both summands are nonnegative and their sum is positive on this interval.

questions.prompt: A rectangle sits inside the upper semicircle x²+y²=25, with its bottom side on the horizontal diameter and its upper corners on the arc. What is its maximum area?
questions.explanation: Write the upper-right corner as (x,√(25−x²)), with full width 2x. Area is A=2x√(25−x²). Its interior derivative vanishes at x²=25/2. Substitution gives A=25, while limiting boundary rectangles have zero area. A: A rectangle cannot simultaneously have full diameter width 10 and height 5. B: This uses half-width times height rather than the full width. C: The half-width and height are both 5/√2, giving area 2xy=25. D: This is the semicircle radius rather than an area.

questions.prompt: A poster must have a printed area of 96 cm². Its margins are 1 cm on each side and 2 cm at the top and bottom. What printed width, in cm, minimizes total paper area?
questions.explanation: Let printed width be x>0 and printed height 96/x. Total area is (x+2)(96/x+4)=104+4x+192/x. Its derivative 4−192/x² changes from negative to positive at x=√48, giving the unique global minimum for positive width. A: This ignores the different total horizontal and vertical margin widths. B: The total-area derivative is negative there, so increasing width would reduce area. C: The total-area derivative is positive there, past the minimum. D: The total area is 104+4x+192/x and its stationary positive width satisfies x²=48.

questions.prompt: Nonnegative real numbers u and v satisfy u+v=10. What is the smallest possible value of u³+v³?
questions.explanation: Set v=10−u with 0≤u≤10. Then F=u³+(10−u)³, and F′=3u²−3(10−u)²=60u−300. It vanishes at u=5, with positive second derivative 60. Endpoint values are 1000 and the interior value is 250. A: The equal values u=v=5 give 125+125. B: This counts only one of the two cubes at the optimum. C: This is an endpoint value when one number is zero. D: This is the fixed sum, not the sum of cubes.

questions.prompt: A total-cost model is C(q)=100+4q+q² dollars for 1≤q≤50. What is the minimum average cost C(q)/q, in dollars per item?
questions.explanation: Average cost is A=100/q+4+q. Its derivative 1−100/q² vanishes at the allowed input 10, changing from negative to positive. Then A(10)=10+4+10=24 dollars/item. Both endpoint values are larger. A: This is the total cost at q=10, not the cost per item. B: Average cost is 100/q+4+q and is minimized at q=10. C: This is the minimizing quantity rather than average cost. D: This omits the fixed-cost-per-item and quadratic contributions.
